chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: Pay on 52nd Street, Oscar Moore's inheritance, and Curtis Mosby's pay
summary: Everyone on 52nd earned $35; Oscar Moore inherited parking lots and quit playing; Mosby paid only the tough.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You mean, all over town, or just the Second Street?

Fifty- Second Street, and the Village, too. Only Nat didn't get his 35, he didn't get paid at all. He had one of these Buick Torpedoes, you know, the torpedoe back, where it's slanted? That was, I'd say, around '41, and anything that he bought, Oscar Moore had to buy something better. Because Oscar had money before he joined Nat. What do you call it, a -- an inheritance. He and his brother inherited some money, from the mother. They lived in Arizona, I think. And it must have been an awful big size. He must have owned a lot of property or something, man. 'Cause he had a lot of money. Then he ends up going with this girl, Oscar Moore, that is, when he left King Cole. He had been going with this girl for quite a while. And she was very loyal to him. And he knew her father. But the father had more of a crush on him than the girl did, because he'd go fishing with the father, you know. Anytime he wanted to go fishing, "oh, have your reel ready, we'll be ready," you know. Then they'd go and talk.

So the father in talking to Oscar, told him, he says, "When I die," he says, "I'm going to will everything to you, 'cause I know you'll take care of my daughter." And this father had parking lots all over Los Angeles proper. Oscar Moore hasn't touched a guitar since. No one knows where he is or how he can be found.
Well, the girl, was that Mamie?
I don't know who she was.
Seems to me his wife's name was Mamie.
I don't know. I sure would like to get in touch with him. Just for old times' sake. And laugh at Curtis Moseby.

I think that he and I got paid mainly because my mother knew Curtis Moseby, and she was a pretty tough customer, you know. And I think Oscar threatened to shoot him if he didn't get his money. So everyone else had to go for the okey-doke.
Curtis Moseby was not reliable so far as pay went?
But yet an awful lot of people worked for him.
Yeah. Everyone else got the business.
